name: veterinary_clinic_system_071_location_performance_dashboard
instruction: Build the monthly multi-location operations dashboard in ops_reports for the org-admin All Locations view. For each of the three locations, create one ops_reports row with report='location_rollup' and the batch code: {location_id, location_name, appointments_total, appointments_today (appointment_date date-prefix equals the episode date), appointments_completed, appointments_no_show, completed_pct (round 100*appointments_completed/appointments_total, 1), no_show_pct (round 100*appointments_no_show/appointments_total, 1), active_patients (patients with status='active' at this location), total_providers, veterinarians (role='veterinarian'), support_staff (all other roles), has_kennel_staff (true iff any provider at that location has role='kennel_attendant'), total_runs (boarding_runs at this location), occupied_runs (status='occupied'), occupancy_pct (round 100*occupied_runs/total_runs, 1), paid_revenue (sum of total_amount on paid invoices at this location), transfers_in (location_transfers with to_location_id=this location), transfers_out (location_transfers with from_location_id=this location)}. Then create one ops_reports row per location with report='location_top_service': {location_id, location_name, top_service_description, top_service_count, top_service_revenue}. The top service is the line-item description that appears most often on paid invoices at that location (tie -> alphabetically first); top_service_count is the number of line items with that description, top_service_revenue is the sum of unit_price*quantity for those line items. Use the appointment's location_id, not the provider's home location, for appointment counts. Use paid invoices only for revenue and top service; do not use billing_estimates. Use the physical boarding_runs table for occupancy, not boarding_reservations. No collection outside ops_reports may be modified.
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: Recompute all per-location dashboard metrics from live collections; exactly one location_rollup row and one location_top_service row per active location, with the correct counts, percentages (within 0.05 pct points), revenue, and top service. Provider counts and appointment counts must be decoupled (provider home location != appointment location in many rows); occupancy must use boarding_runs, not reservations. Every aggregate verified by both a raw-row Python pass and an independent SQL pass.

checks.expect: appointments_total/today/completed/no_show and paid_revenue/top_service recomputed by raw-row filter and SQL GROUP BY and agree with each other and the written rows

hazards: Provider home location vs appointment location mismatch: 364 of 548 appointments have a provider whose location_id differs from the appointment's location_id (e.g. appointment id=1 is at location 1 but provider_id=3, whose home location is 2). Counting appointments by provider home location would over/under-count every location.

Boarding occupancy must come from boarding_runs.status='occupied'. boarding_reservations has 5 checked_in rows at location 1 only, but the physical run board has 5 occupied runs at location 1, 0 at locations 2 and 3 (boarding_runs K01-K05 are occupied at loc 1). Using reservation counts as capacity or occupancy produces wrong percentages at every location.
Paid revenue and top service must use billing_invoices with status='paid'. billing_estimates and draft/sent invoices are not cash revenue and must not be counted.

The top service per location is not uniform: location 1 = 'Ear cytology' (33 paid line items, revenue 8305.00), location 2 = 'Vaccination – rabies' (37 items, 8911.00), location 3 = 'Boarding (3 nights)' (35 items, 7740.00). An agent that picks the global top service or uses all invoices puts the wrong description in each row.

appointments_today depends on the live episode_date, which jitters per episode. The seed has appointments on 2026-09-04, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-01, etc., so the today count is not a constant and must be derived live from the nonce.
active_patients must use patients.status='active'; patient id=27 has status='transferred' and must not be counted at its home location.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses location-level appointment flow, boarding occupancy, provider staffing, paid revenue, top service, and transfer volume into a single dashboard, with the explicit decoupling of provider home location from appointment location and the physical-run-board occupancy source. Dual-path verification across six collections.
